goal: Make every non-terminal /immune-brain:drive pause (user wait, blocked batch, host_failure, review_incomplete or rejection, the consecutive-stop limit, native-failure limit, Pi interrupt) suspend the enrolled session without revoking its entry token on the same bound (workspace, batch_id | run_id) across Claude Code, Pi, and Antigravity; revoke only on the closed list (settled run, SessionEnd, explicit cancel, /draw-up or /clarify entry, workspace or bound-identity drift); clear suspension and native_failures on the next plain user prompt; reset native_failures on any applied native operation; and amend ADR 0025 §3/§6 while keeping Host Native Gates intact, per D1 of docs/specs/workflow-friction-simplification.spec.md.

acceptance.assertion: Source BR-DEC-1; meet D1.1 and BR-SCN-1 in docs/specs/workflow-friction-simplification.spec.md. Agreed seam: tests/run-continuation.test.ts, tests/claude-run-continuation.test.ts, tests/pi-run-continuation.test.ts, tests/antigravity-assurance-conformance.test.ts, tests/claude-phase-entry-gate.test.ts, tests/pi-phase-entry-gate.test.ts. Done looks like: every non-terminal pause of an enrolled batch or task run (user wait, any blocked batch, host_failure, review_incomplete or rejection, the consecutive-stop limit, the native-failure limit, and a Pi interrupted turn) suspends continuation without revoking entry_token, suspension stops automatic continuation, and the next plain-text non-cancelling/non-planning user prompt clears suspension so subsequent immune-brain MCP calls reach their Native Gates without run_entry_required across Claude, Pi, and Antigravity; docs/adr/0025-run-entry-decision-hosting.md §3/§6 documents suspension versus revocation. Negative: a settled run, SessionEnd, explicit cancel (releasesRunBinding), /draw-up or /clarify entry, and workspace or bound batch/task identity drift still revoke entry_token and refuse subsequent token-backed MCP calls with run_entry_required; Native Gates remain required.

Source BR-REQ-1; meet D1.2 in docs/specs/workflow-friction-simplification.spec.md. Agreed seam: tests/run-continuation.test.ts, tests/claude-run-continuation.test.ts, tests/antigravity-assurance-conformance.test.ts. Done looks like: any applied native operation (including start_unattended_batch with state === "started") resets metadata.native_failures to 0, and the next plain user prompt after a suspension also resets it, so two failures followed by a success allow two more failures before NATIVE_FAILURE_LIMIT. Negative: three consecutive failed or non-applied native operations with no intervening success suspend the session (no automatic continuation) without revoking entry_token.
